claim: Kaminski & Lo (J. Financial Markets 2014) find on daily index-futures data that, at longer sampling frequencies, certain stop-loss policies can raise expected return while substantially reducing volatility (applied to buy-and-hold; futures, not options).
quote: At longer sampling frequencies, certain stop-loss policies can increase expected return while substantially reducing volatility, consistent with their objectives in practical applications.
title: When do stop-loss rules stop losses? (MIT DSpace abstract)

claim: Lei & Li (Financial Services Review) find that, on individual common stocks once returns are extended to simulated future paths, stop-loss strategies neither reduce nor increase losses relative to buy-and-hold; value lies mainly in risk reduction (stocks; transfer to options unproven).
quote: Our results indicate that these strategies neither reduce nor increase investors' losses relative to a buy-and-hold strategy once we extend security returns from past realizations to possible future paths.
title: The value of stop loss strategies (FSR)

claim: In a practitioner test (daily bars, 3 futures markets incl. mini S&P, 4 strategies, past 5 years, slippage and commission included, in-sample), the author found no stop beat both the ATR stop and the dollar stop, and the ATR stop beat the dollar stop 66% of the time with many profit factors very similar. Futures; transfer to options unproven.
quote: The ATR Stop beats the Dollar Stop 66% of the time, although many of the resulting profit factors are extremely similar to each other.
title: Dollar Stop Losses Vs. Volatility Stop Losses

claim: Same practitioner test: the 'No Stop' baseline was better than either ATR or dollar stops (futures, daily bars, ~5 years).
quote: The “No Stop” Case is better than either the ATR Stop or the Dollar Stop.
title: Dollar Stop Losses Vs. Volatility Stop Losses

claim: In a 1DTE SPX iron-condor backtest (2022-04-01 to 2025-12-31, short premium, not long options), about 50% of max-loss stop-outs would have expired profitable if held, and nearly 70% of forced exits would have recovered; stops lock in intraday drawdowns.
quote: Roughly 50% of max-loss trades would have expired profitably if held to expiration. For forced exits, nearly 70% would have recovered.
title: Distribution and Regime Effects in a 1DTE Options Strategy

claim: Search snippet only: Fan & Zhang report trailing stop net Sharpe about 1.28 vs 0.92 for fixed stop in commodity factors 1983-2022 (commodities; transfer to options unproven).
quote: From 1983 to 2022, commodity factors on average, with a fixed-stop (trailing-stop) generate a net Sharpe ratio of 0.92 (1.28).
title: Fan and Zhang, risk management of commodity factors

claim: Search snippet only: Lei & Li tested stop thresholds of 5, 10 or 20 daily-return standard deviations on US stocks, holding periods 3-12 months; trailing stops tend to reduce return standard deviation (stocks; vol-scaled stop example).
quote: stop-loss thresholds of 5, 10 or 20 daily return standard deviations
title: CXO Advisory summary of Lei & Li
